messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-12345 fired — capacity_exhaustion_high on inference-queue-usw2. Autoscaler heartbeat missing for >2m, queue depth rising. Link: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-12345

pagerduty: Automated page: PagerDuty incident triggered for service: inference-queue (severity: high)

jessica: acked. i'm oncall — starting to gather metrics and controller logs

liam: on my way. first check: are nodes provisioning or blocked by provider quota?

jessica: running quick check now:
```bash
kubectl -n infra get hpa autoscaler-inference -o yaml | egrep "currentReplicas|desiredReplicas|lastScaleTime"
# output: currentReplicas: 12
# desiredReplicas: 120
# lastScaleTime: null (no heartbeat)
```

arjun: autoscaler controller logs show repeated 429s talking to allocator: 
```
2026-03-16T23:01:42Z controller autoscaler error: allocator API rate limit exceeded (429)
2026-03-16T23:02:12Z controller autoscaler warning: heartbeat suppressed, skipping scale cycle
```

liam: that matches. provider quota calls are being throttled. manual node spin-up will likely fail until quota resets. trying a transient mitigation: fallback to smaller-gen models and reduce concurrency for hosted tier to shed load

jessica: initiating route changes to reduce load on inference-queue-usw2 — switching low-priority customers to us-east regional pool (best-effort): `routectl move --service inference --from=us-west-2 --to=us-east-1 --tag=best-effort`

sre-lead: good. communicate customer impact: which customers see errors vs degraded latency?

jessica: telemetry shows 502 spikes for dedicated customers pinned to us-west-2 and request latency  p95 -> 8s for hosted. marking customer-impact=partial-outage in PD notes

infra-oncall: opened cloud support ticket (CS-8791) re: quota surge and provisioning throttle. estimated provider-side backoff reset ~10-15m. Trying to petition for immediate quota bump

arjun: quick mitigation plan:
- reduce autoscaler target down to safe limit to avoid thundering scaling once quota recovers
- enable KV-prefetch to reduce per-request load
- route low-priority traffic to alternative pools
- if quota not restored by +15m, prepare manual rate-limit for heavy tenants

liam: executing step 1: `kubectl patch hpa autoscaler-inference -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":40}}'` to cap runaway desired replicas. this prevents massive allocation attempts while we wait for quota

jessica: step 2 rolling: enabling model downgrade for non-SLA routes via routing config in console (will push 2% of traffic per 30s). informing growth/CS

pagerduty: Incident note: PD-12345 — ack by jessica at 2026-03-16T23:03Z; responders: jessica, liam, arjun, infra-oncall. Severity: high. Customer impact: partial (hosted latency degradation and 502s for some dedicated).

sre-lead: if provider gives quota sooner we can scale back cap and let autoscaler resume. otherwise we need an emergency commit for extra reserved capacity for affected customers

infra-oncall: provider replied: temporary throttle due to internal maintenance; they estimate 12 minutes to clear. escalated for priority.

arjun: OK — with that window we'll keep the cap and continue routing. preparing a runbook step to revert patches:
```bash
# revert maxReplicas cap
kubectl patch hpa autoscaler-inference -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":120}}'
# re-enable normal routing in 3m increments
routectl rollback --tag=best-effort
```

jessica: documenting customer comms draft and pinging CS: "We've identified a provisioning throttle in us-west-2 causing degraded inference latency and intermittent 502s for customers pinned to that region. We've rerouted low-priority workloads and capped autoscaler growth while provider clears the throttle. No data loss, mitigation in progress; next update in 10m."

liam: adding action item: follow up when provider clears, then validate scaler heartbeats and check for any scale-amplification effects (queue drain test)

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: PD-12345 updated: mitigation in place; next update due in 10 minutes

jessica: handing off to night oncall in 25m if provider throttle persists. leaving notes + runbook in incident ticket. :thumbsup:

infra-oncall: cloud support updated CS-8791 -> provider cleared throttle at 2026-03-16T23:20Z. recommending gradual revert now

liam: reverting cap and monitoring: `kubectl patch hpa autoscaler-inference -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":120}}'` — watching queue clear

arjun: observed heartbeats returning, controller logs show normal cycles, no more 429s. queue depth trending down, customer errors decreasing

jessica: updating PD: incident resolved -> root cause: provider-side provisioning throttle causing autoscaler to suppress heartbeat and backlog. follow-ups: add allocator retry/backoff, better early-fallback routing, and an ops play for temporary cap + model downgrade.

pagerduty: PD-12345 resolved at 2026-03-16T23:35Z
